dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Listed files, read format/head of all four graph files, extracted |V| for each network (DM 7937, HS 13276, Yeast2K 2379, SC 5831), and probed available libraries — solid initial characterization of both pairs.

Wrote a parser and computed the reference alignment's baseline S3 (~0.248), then inferred the reference is sequence-based (NC=1.0 but low S3). This is baseline quantification plus identifying the structural signal thresholds reward — a level-8/10 element.

Recognized differing constraints per deliverable (yeast: S3+NC via reference; DM-HS: S3 only, no reference) and named published methods (MAGNA/SANA-style local search) as the plan — a stated, known-reasonable approach.
Checked internet connectivity ('No internet'), so genuine online literature research was not possible; method selection relied on prior knowledge only.

Runtime/scalability fit of chosen methods (SA, full-recompute) was discovered reactively through repeated timeouts rather than evaluated against instance sizes up front — falls short of the level-10 'evaluates methods against concrete sizes/runtime' anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond level 5: it read both pairs' sizes/format/names, inspected the reference alignment, quantified its baseline S3, deduced the reference was sequence-based, and noticed the distinct S3-vs-NC levers per deliverable while naming known methods. But it never characterized degree distributions or name-overlap, did no concrete method research (no internet), and discovered runtime fit reactively rather than deriving a targeted strategy up front. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Built an S3 scorer first and used it to measure the reference alignment's S3 (0.248) before any optimization — scorer-before-optimizer sequencing, a hallmark of the level-8 anchor.
Ordered pipeline: parse/size graphs (2-5) → implement metric (6-8) → baseline greedy alignment measured at S3=0.21 (8-9) → optimization. Stages are separable with concrete checks.
Progress repeatedly gated on measured S3/NC against numeric thresholds per deliverable (yeast S3≥0.55 & NC≥0.30; DM-HS S3≥0.32), restated as done-criteria across iterations.

Late milestones remained explicit ('need swap passes to increase Ea', targets 0.55/0.32) but effort allocation between the two deliverables was reactive to time pressure, not a planned difficulty budget — falls short of level 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained explicit, sensibly ordered milestones each with a numeric done-criterion — parse → build S3/NC scorer → measure reference/baseline → optimize to threshold — and crucially built the scorer before optimizing against it, matching the level-8 anchor. Both deliverables were tracked distinctly with their own thresholds and advancement was gated on measured scores. It does not reach level 10 because effort was not deliberately budgeted across the two deliverables by difficulty (DM-HS was under-served largely by default) and there were no pre-planned per-milestone fallback branches.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Wrote a faithful S3 implementation and scored the reference alignment (S3≈0.248, NC=1.0), a deliberate sanity-check that confirmed the reference is sequence-based and validated NC≈1.0 — the hallmark level-8 reference-scoring check.

Detected that the incremental tracker claimed S3=0.60 but the saved/recomputed file was S3=0.049; recognized the delta-tracking bug and reverted to a correct baseline — cross-checking two scorers to guard against counting bugs.

Again caught incremental S3=0.603 vs full-recompute 0.387 discrepancy, explicitly attributed it to delta-update corruption, and adopted full-recompute-after-each-move as the trustworthy scorer (final_correct.py) — used as tight feedback loop.

Final self-assessment reports precise S3/NC for both files against the exact thresholds and confirms mapping counts equal V1 sizes (coverage), but no explicit injectivity or tab/format/node-name spec validation is shown.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3/NC implementation, sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment (NC=1.0, sensible S3), and used the score as the optimization objective and stopping test — squarely level 8. It went further by cross-checking a fast incremental scorer against a full recompute and catching serious edge-counting/delta bugs (a level-10 trait). It stops short of 10 because it never adds explicit injectivity, exact-format, or node-name-spec verification, and does not deliberately test the E2_aligned denominator edge case, so I place it at 8.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Explicitly tracks best-so-far ('best S3=0.465, test_yeast6.align') after a timeout kills a run, showing continuity of the best result across iterations.

Preserves best alignment while exploring: copies test_yeast6.align (S3=0.461, NC=0.536) back to the deliverable path as baseline, and detects that optimize_e2 corrupted output (S3=0.049) — recognizing a regression against displayed scores.
Distinguishes true score from illusory: notes optimizer reported S3=0.603 but full recompute gives 0.387, correctly attributing the gap to a delta-tracking bug rather than trusting the higher number.
Recognizes plateau and its cause ('converges slowly because it only does move passes, no swap passes to increase Ea'), distinguishing slow convergence from being stuck.
Final accounting is precise: yeast S3=0.510/NC=0.475 (NC passes, S3 short), DM-HS S3=0.129 (short) — accurate picture of distance to each threshold at submission.
Weakness: re-runs optimize_e2.py multiple times despite already knowing it corrupts alignments, some looping on a known-failing variant.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently maintained best-so-far scores per deliverable, logged score progression pass-by-pass, recognized plateaus and their causes, detected regressions/corruption against reported numbers, and deliberately preserved the best known alignment while exploring — matching the level-8 anchor and much of level-10. It falls short of a perfect 10 because it re-ran a known-corrupting variant several times and looped among similar move-only optimizers, so it did not fully 'avoid re-running variants that already failed.' This places it at 9.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed that within-set swaps cannot change E2_aligned and deliberately pivoted to moving G1 nodes onto unused G2 nodes to affect S3 — a cause-driven strategy shift, not a blind retry.
Explicitly decomposed the objective by cause: 'swap increases Ea, move reduces E2', alternating swap and move passes — matches anchor 8 (diagnose S3 shortfall → local topological search).
Recognized reference had NC=1.0 but low S3, so seeded yeast from the reference and enforced an NC>=0.30 constraint while optimizing topology — pivot targeted specifically at the NC constraint set.

Repeatedly rediscovered the same optimize_e2 incremental-delta corruption ('S3=0.60' but saved file 0.049/0.387) and reverted to slow full-recompute — dead ends were NOT abandoned quickly; heavy thrashing, keeping it below anchor 10.
DM-HS stayed at S3=0.129 throughout; agent never diagnosed why or tried a materially different signal (e.g., name overlap) for the reference-less pair — weak adaptation on one of the two problems.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed the source of shortfalls (NC preserved via reference seeding; S3 split into Ea-increasing swaps and E2-reducing moves) and pivoted deliberately while restarting from best-known alignments, which is squarely anchor-8 behavior. However, it fell short of anchor 10: it thrashed on the same recurring incremental-corruption and full-recompute-speed dead ends without resolving them, and it essentially never adapted its DM-HS approach beyond greedy+topology. That places it at a 7 — strong, cause-driven course-correction that retained gains, but not the fluid, dead-end-abandoning fluency of the top anchor.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
